newsitem.title: UK: Abbey sees "attractive" final bid for ScotAm.
newsitem.headline: Abbey sees "attractive" final bid for ScotAm.

text.p: Abbey National Plc said on Wednesday it would ensure its final offer for mutually-owned life assurer Scottish Amicable would be "extremely attractive" once it had access to all the financial information on the insurer.

"Once we have access to full financial information we are sure that our final offer will be extremely attractive to Scottish Amicable's policyholders, management and staff," said deputy chief executive Charles Toner in a statement.

Last week Abbey made an offer between 1.1 billion and 1.4 billion stg for the life assurer. Abbey's offer entailed a minimum of 400 million stg to policyholders and an immediate investment into the funds of with-profit policyholders of between 700 million to one billion stg.
Abbey chief executive Charles Toner said that the bank's 400 million goodwill offer was a minimum level and that it would pay whatever was agreed to be the embedded value.

Earlier on Wednesday Prudential Corp Plc mounted a rival bid of 1.9 billion stg for ScotAm. The Prudential bid came just days after Abbey National interrupted ScotAm's plans to shed its mutual status and eventually float on the stock exchange.
ScotAm has said it would seek competing offers from other parties and has postponed sending out a circular on its own flotation plans for at least two weeks.
The life assurer said it had had interest from both overseas and British firms and would talk to the interested parties on an equal basis with the same information available to everybody.
Toner said, "We are pleased to learn that Scottish Amicable will be considering our offer. We look forward to discussions with them."
